history.summary: Founded in 1694 CE (1000 Mallabda) by Malla king Durjan Singha Dev, per the foundation plaque. A square eka-ratna (single-pinnacle) temple in Bengal temple architecture, faced south, built of brick on a laterite plinth and famed for terracotta plaques depicting Krishna-lila, Dashavatara, Ramayana and Mahabharata scenes. Local legend holds that the deity Madanmohan defended the Malla king against the Bargi (Maratha) invaders. One account claims an 1820 earthquake destroyed and replaced the temple (unverified). Conflict: Wikipedia states no worship is currently conducted and the ASI preserves it; Bankura tourism and travel accounts describe it as an active temple with regular Vaishnava puja — verify.

name: Madanmohan Temple
town_description: Bishnupur (Vishnupur) is the historic capital of the Malla kings in Bankura district, West Bengal, famed as a terracotta temple town: its 17th-18th century brick temples, Baluchari sarees, terracotta craft and classical music heritage make it one of the state's best-known heritage destinations.

travel.airport: Nearest airports: Kazi Nazrul Islam Airport, Durgapur (~90 km) and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~140 km)
travel.railway: Bishnupur Junction railway station (in town), well connected to Kolkata
travel.road: ~142 km / ~4 hours by road from Kolkata; state and private buses serve the town
